name: Physics
notes: The department page writes course codes as PHY / MTH; the registrar catalog this app is built from uses PHYS / MATH, which is the form used here.
At least a 2.0 (C) average in astronomy, physics and mathematics courses must be maintained. All course choices must be approved by the undergraduate physics advisor.
The BA is the broader, more flexible degree; students aiming at graduate school in physics should consider the BS.

The 'eight additional credit hours' group is modeled as two 200-300 level technical courses in physics, astronomy, mathematics, or another science/engineering department - the page states credit hours rather than a course count.
Graduate-level courses generally cannot be substituted for undergraduate core requirements.

requirementGroups.label: Pre-concentration: calculus sequence
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: One of the following calculus sequences: MTH 161, 162, 164, and 165; MTH 171, 172, 173, and 174

requirementGroups.label: Pre-concentration: introductory physics (3)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Three introductory physics courses: PHY 121 or PHY 141; PHY 122 or PHY 142; PHY 123 or PHY 143

requirementGroups.label: Core physics courses
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: PHY 217: Electricity and Magnetism I; PHY 235W: Classical Mechanics; PHY 237: Quantum Mechanics of Physical Systems

requirementGroups.label: One further core course
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: One of the following: PHY 218: Electricity and Magnetism II; PHY 227: Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics; PHY 243W: Advanced Experimental Techniques I; PHY 245W: The Advanced Nuclear Science Education Laboratory; PHY 246: Quantum Theory

requirementGroups.label: One 200-300 level physics or astronomy course
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: One four-credit 200-300 level physics and/or astronomy course.

requirementGroups.label: Eight additional credit hours of 200-300 level technical courses
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Eight additional credit hours, which can be 200- or 300-level technical courses in: Physics; Astronomy; Mathematics; Another science or engineering
requirementGroups.note: Stated as 8 credit hours; modeled as two 4-credit courses.
